question: A Platform Administrator deactivates an agent to add a new topic and action. What happens to any ongoing user conversations with the agent?
optionA: The agent will pause the conversation and resume once reactivated.
optionB: The agent will continue conversations using the deactivated agent until reactivated.
optionC: The agent window automatically closes to prevent new messages.
optionD: The agent will send a system error message as a response to any new messages.
explanation:
The agent sending a system error message as a response to any new messages is what happens, and Activate or Deactivate Your Agent states the behaviour outright: "Deactivating an agent interrupts any ongoing user conversations. Users aren't notified that an agent is deactivated. The agent sends the system error message as a response to any messages." That is exactly what the keyed option describes.
So deactivation is not a graceful drain. There is no version pinning that lets sessions started before the change finish on the old configuration, and nothing pauses and resumes. A user mid-conversation simply gets the system error message back, with no explanation that anything has changed.
The window does not close either. If the agent uses the Agentforce panel, the panel stays available until the user closes it and cannot be reopened until the agent is active again; on an Enhanced Chat deployment the chat window still appears, but the agent does not join the conversation.
The practical consequence is the reason Salesforce documents agent versions: to change an agent without taking the live one out of service, work on a separate version rather than deactivating the active one.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (the agent pauses and resumes on reactivation) — nothing pauses and resumes; the conversation is interrupted and the user gets an error.
Option B (conversations continue on the deactivated agent) — there is no version pinning that lets existing sessions finish on the old configuration.
Option C (the agent window closes automatically) — the panel or chat window stays where it is; the agent simply stops responding.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_setup_activate_deactivate.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The key said ongoing conversations continue on the deactivated agent until it is reactivated. The documentation says the opposite - deactivating interrupts ongoing conversations and the agent responds to any further messages with the system error message, which is the option the key had listed as wrong.

question: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks is setting up a new Salesforce instance. The business requirements mandate that the marketers are given access to opportunities in order to maintain the campaign relationships on each opportunity. The administrator decides to assign the Marketing User profile. What should the administrator do next to achieve this requirement?
optionA: Edit the object permissions to include Opportunity.
optionB: Add a custom permission set to include Opportunity.
optionC: Edit the role to enable Sales access.
optionD: Configure the assigned apps to include Opportunity.
explanation:
Editing the object permissions to include Opportunity is the next step. Profiles define object-level security (create, read, edit, delete), and the standard Marketing User profile does not include full edit access to Opportunity by default, since marketing roles are traditionally focused on Leads and Campaigns. If the org uses a custom profile based on the Marketing User template, the admin edits its object permissions to include Read and Edit for Opportunities, so marketers can view the records and update the Primary Campaign Source field. A permission set could also grant this access, but the question has the administrator configuring the profile itself, and adjusting its object permissions is the direct way to align the user's capabilities with the requirement.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (add a custom permission set for Opportunity) — a valid way to grant object access in general, but the administrator has just chosen the profile route, and the direct next step is to give that profile the missing object permission.
Option C (edit the role to enable Sales access) — roles govern record visibility through the hierarchy; they do not grant object permissions on Opportunity.
Option D (configure the assigned apps to include Opportunity) — app assignment puts a tab in front of the user; it does not grant the object permission needed to read or edit opportunity records.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_object_perms.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Platform Administrator has been asked to change the data type of an auto number to a text field. What should the administrator be aware of before changing the field?
optionA: Existing field values will remain unchanged.
optionB: Changing Auto Number field to Text is prevented.
optionC: Existing field values will be deleted.
optionD: Existing field values will be converted.
explanation:
Existing field values remaining unchanged is what the administrator should be aware of: converting an auto-number field to text keeps the data. Considerations for Converting the Field Type of a Custom Field says it in the data-type table: "If you convert an auto-number field into a text field, the data in that field remains unchanged." The generated values stay in place as ordinary text.
What stops is the generation. Once the field is text, Salesforce no longer assigns the next number on insert, so anything created afterwards needs the value supplied.
Read the article carefully here, because its two halves look contradictory. The general data-loss list includes "Changing from Auto Number to any other type" - that covers auto number to number, to date, and so on. Text is the documented exception, called out separately.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (the change is prevented) — the conversion is allowed; the article documents it explicitly.
Option C (existing values are deleted) — the documented behaviour is the opposite: the data in that field remains unchanged.
Option D (existing values are converted) — nothing is transformed; the generated strings are kept as they are, now as ordinary text.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.notes_on_changing_custom_field_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A sales team is having difficulty understanding which stage their opportunity is in and what the company sales process requires of them in that stage. Which feature should a Platform Administrator implement to help the sales team quickly determine where they are in the sales process and what is required of them?
explanation:
Opportunity Sales Path (Path) is the feature that shows the sales team where they are in the process and what is required of them. It is a visual representation of the stages that shows the current stage prominently at the top of the record and lets administrators define Key Fields and Guidance for Success for every stage - specific steps, tips and links to company resources that explain exactly what a rep needs to do to move the deal to the next phase.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Reports & Dashboards) — provide data about the pipeline, not the contextual stage-by-stage guidance on the record.
Option C (Big Deal Alerts) — send a notification when an opportunity crosses an amount or probability; they say nothing about the sales process.
Option D (List Views) — show which stage each record is in, but offer no guidance on what the stage requires.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.path_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Platform Administrator is building an agent to help an ecommerce support team. The agent needs to call an action, named updateShippingAddress, that modifies a customer's shipping address in the system. Which set of Action Instructions should the administrator use for the updateShippingAddress action, according to best practices?
optionA: "Use this to update shipping information. It's used for any changes to a customer's address in the system."
optionB: "This action updates the customer's shipping address. It is to be used when a user wants to change their address. Only use this when a customer does not have an active order in the system."
optionC: "This action allows for the changing of a shipping address, and the goal is to make sure the address is current and accurate."
optionD: "Updates the shipping address for a customer order. The goal of the action is to modify the address on a customer's record. The agent should only use this action when the user explicitly requests to change their address."
explanation:
The instruction set that names the action, states its goal and adds an explicit guardrail - "Updates the shipping address for a customer order. The goal of the action is to modify the address on a customer's record. The agent should only use this action when the user explicitly requests to change their address." - is the strongest, according to Agentforce best practices. Action instructions must be specific about the action's purpose, the expected goal and the conditions under which it should be triggered; option D defines all three, which prevents the AI from accidentally triggering a data change on a vague inquiry and ensures the LLM understands the why and the when of the action.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A ("Use this to update shipping information… any changes to a customer's address") — vague on purpose and open-ended on scope; it gives no goal and no condition for when to trigger the action.
Option B (only use when the customer has no active order) — well structured but adds a constraint the business has not stated; it is more restrictive than necessary unless the logic specifically forbids updates during active orders.
Option C ("allows for the changing of a shipping address… make sure the address is current and accurate") — states a goal but no trigger condition, so the agent has no guardrail against changing an address the user did not ask to change.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_instructions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Ursa Major Solar wants to automatically notify a manager about any cases awaiting a response from an agent for more than 2 hours after case creation. Which feature should a Platform Administrator use to fulfill this requirement?
explanation:
A Case Escalation Rule is the dedicated tool for time-based notifications and reassignments in Service Cloud. The Platform Administrator sets an escalation rule entry that triggers when a case is older than 2 hours and meets specific status criteria (for example Status = New), configured to send an email notification to a manager or a distribution list, so management is alerted to potential SLA breaches.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Assignment Rule) — only runs when a case is first created; it has no time-elapsed trigger.
Option C (Formula field) — can calculate elapsed time but cannot send a notification.
Option D (Omni-Channel Supervisor) — real-time monitoring of agents and queues; it does not send automated alerts on a time threshold.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.rules_escalation_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A VP of sales needs to report on records owned by individuals in various parts of the role hierarchy. The organization-wide default is set to Private. What should a Platform Administrator configure to achieve this?
explanation:
Sharing Rules are what the Platform Administrator configures. When an object's organization-wide default is Private, users see only the records they own or that are shared with them; the role hierarchy grants upward visibility (managers see what subordinates own) but not lateral visibility across different branches. Sharing rules create exceptions to the Private OWD based on record ownership or criteria - for example an owner-based rule that shares all records owned by the East Coast Sales role with the VP of Sales or a public group the VP belongs to - which is a scalable way to grant the visibility needed for reporting without making the data public to the whole company.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Field-Level Security) — controls which fields a user can see on records they already have access to; it grants no record access.
Option C (Permission Sets) — grant object and system permissions, not access to specific records owned by others in a Private model.
Option D (Restriction Rules) — do the opposite of what is needed: they narrow the records a user can see, never widen them.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_owd_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.security_sharing_rules_criteria.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) has a new Platform Administrator who is asked to put together a memo detailing Salesforce usage to budget for upcoming license purchases. Where should the administrator go to find out what type of licenses CK has purchased and how many are available?
optionA: Usage-based entitlements related list in company information
optionB: Search for licenses types in setup
optionC: User licenses related list in company information
explanation:
The User Licenses related list in Company Information is where to find what licenses CK has purchased and how many are available. The Company Information page in Setup is the source of truth for an org's high-level metadata and licensing; its User Licenses related list shows every license type purchased (Salesforce, Salesforce Platform and so on), the total seats allocated, the seats in use and the remaining available licenses - the first place to look for budgeting and capacity planning.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Usage-based entitlements related list) — tracks limited-resource features such as login minutes or credits, not standard seat-based user licenses.
Option B (search for license types in Setup) — Setup search finds pages, not a consolidated summary of the total license pool.
Option D (User Management Settings) — holds user-interface toggles for user management; it lists no licenses.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_license_types_view.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question:
A new agent is being developed to help customer service reps process customer requests for a replacement product. The agent needs to call an action that takes two inputs:
* productId: An 18 character ID for the product being replaced.
* reasonCode: A three-digit code representing the reason for the replacement.
Which set of agent instructions should a Platform Administrator use for these inputs, according to best practices for Agentforce instructions?
optionA: Instructions for productId: "The 18 character ID of the product." Instructions for reasonCode: "A numerical code."
optionB: Instructions for productId: "The product ID. Retrieve this from the conversation history or the user's input." Instructions for reasonCode: "The three-digit replacement reason. This is required when the product ID is present."
optionC: Instructions for productId: "ID from the product record." Instructions for reasonCode: "Code for the reason."
optionD: Instructions for productId: "The 18 character ID of the product. Retrieve this from the conversation history or the user's input. Required." Instructions for reasonCode: "A three-digit code that specifies the reason for replacement. This is required only when the product ID is present."
explanation:
The instruction set that states the format, the source and the dependency for both inputs - "The 18 character ID of the product. Retrieve this from the conversation history or the user's input. Required." and "A three-digit code that specifies the reason for replacement. This is required only when the product ID is present." - is the best choice. Effective Agentforce input instructions must be explicit about the data format, the source of the data and the requirement on the input; option D provides all three for the LLM, which prevents the agent from guessing or passing incomplete data to the underlying Salesforce action. High-quality instructions act as a contract between the agent's natural-language understanding and the structured data requirements of the system.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A ("The 18 character ID of the product." / "A numerical code.") — states a format for one input and almost nothing for the other; no source, no requirement.
Option B (product ID from conversation or input; reason required when the product ID is present) — better, but it omits the explicit Required tag and the format details (18 characters, three digits) that option D includes.
Option C ("ID from the product record." / "Code for the reason.") — too vague to guide the model; no format, source or requirement for either input.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_instructions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A sales manager at Cloud Kicks would like a dashboard to emphasize some important data and tell a more compelling data story to the sales reps. How should a Platform Administrator achieve this for the sales manager?
optionB: Assign a new Task to each rep.
explanation:
A Text Widget is how to make the dashboard tell a more compelling data story. In Lightning dashboards, text widgets let administrators add descriptive text, titles and custom narratives directly alongside the visualisations - context, an explanation of why a chart matters, instructions or a motivational message - turning a collection of raw charts into a guided analytical experience that highlights trends and calls out specific goals.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (assign a new Task to each rep) — a communication method; it changes nothing on the dashboard.
Option C (use the Highlights Panel) — a feature of record pages, not of dashboards.
Option D (send out a mass email) — like the task, a way to talk to reps, not a way to enhance the dashboard's narrative.

question: A Platform Administrator is designing a prompt template for a new agent. The agent's purpose is to help service reps troubleshoot technical issues by providing concise, step-by-step instructions. Based on best practices for creating effective prompts, which approach should the administrator use when writing this prompt?
optionA: Write a detailed prompt with multiple nested conditions to cover all the major troubleshooting scenarios.
optionB: Use specific technical terms and abbreviations to ensure the AI understands the specialised domain.
optionC: Focus on providing high-level, theoretical concepts so the AI has the flexibility to respond creatively.
optionD: Use natural, easy-to understand language and clear, concise instructions to guide the AI's behavior.
explanation:
Using natural, easy-to-understand language and clear, concise instructions to guide the AI's behaviour is the approach best practices prescribe. Effective Agentforce prompts focus on clarity and simplicity so the LLM follows instructions accurately and reasons through the task without being confused by overly complex logic; direct instructions such as "Summarize the issue in three bullet points" are more effective than broad guidelines.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a detailed prompt with multiple nested conditions) — nested logic is exactly what confuses a model; the guidance is to keep instructions simple and direct.
Option B (specialised technical terms and abbreviations) — jargon and abbreviations can produce unexpected results when the LLM interprets them differently in different contexts.
Option C (high-level theoretical concepts for creative flexibility) — produces vague or "creative" answers, which is the opposite of the specific, actionable steps technical troubleshooting needs.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_topics_instructions.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_instructions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which two actions should a Platform Administrator perform with Case escalation rules?
explanation:
Sending email notifications and reassigning the case are the two actions, and Escalation Actions documents what an escalation action can actually do as a short list: reassign the case, and notify people.
Reassignment sends the case to another support rep or to a support queue - the usual pattern being Level 1 handing off to a Level 2 queue when it has not been resolved in time. Notification is by email, and it can go to the new assignee, to the current case owner, and to as many as five further addresses.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (change the Case Priority) — not an escalation action; priority is something you set with a field update from other automation.
Option C (reopen the Case) — not an escalation action either; reopening a case is a manual or flow-driven change of status.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.rules_escalation_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Sales managers would like to know what could be implemented to surface important values based on the stage of the opportunity? Which tool should a Platform Administrator use to meet this requirement?
explanation:
Path Key Fields are the tool for surfacing important values based on the opportunity's stage. The Opportunity Path guides reps through the sales cycle, and for each individual stage the administrator can define Key Fields - Budget and Decision Maker in Discovery, say, and Contract Terms and Discount Percentage in Negotiation - so reps are prompted to enter and review the most relevant data at exactly the right point in the process, organised at the top of the record and tied to the sales methodology.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Workflow Rules) — a legacy automation tool; it cannot modify the user interface or surface fields.
Option C (Opportunity Processes) — a sales process defines which stages a record type uses; it does not surface fields per stage.
Option D (Dynamic Forms) — can show or hide fields on the record page by condition, but it does not organise stage-specific values at the top of the record the way Path Key Fields do; Path is the feature built for this.

question: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks has created a screen flow to help service reps ask the same set of questions when customers call in with issues. This screen should be visible from cases. How should the administrator distribute the screen flow?
explanation:
A Lightning Page is how to distribute the screen flow. A screen flow reaches users by being placed somewhere, and for a flow that has to run in the context of a specific case, that somewhere is the Case Lightning record page. In Lightning App Builder you drag the Flow component onto the page and pick the flow; from then on reps see it beside the case details, with the record's id available to the flow.

Option A (Page Layout) — the wrong instrument: it governs fields, related lists and actions, not Lightning components.
Option B (Home Page) — would run the flow without any case in context, which defeats the point.
Option D (Component Filter) — component visibility filters decide when a component shows, not how a flow gets onto a page at all.

question: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks received a request from the head of sales operations to create a process in which opportunities must be validated by specific team leaders based on a mix of criteria. When the administrator analysed the list of criteria, they found that there were 30 potential sets of criteria that would identify the proper person to route the request to. How should the administrator fulfill this request?
optionA: Create a button on the opportunity that brings up an email template to send to the correct leader.
optionB: Create an approval process with specific entry criteria and approval steps for each of the sets of criteria specified.
optionC: Create a record triggered flow orchestration to properly route the requests.
optionD: Use a screen flow to allow the seller to input the criteria in a form that is then sent to the appropriate leader.
explanation:
Creating an approval process with specific entry criteria and approval steps for each set of criteria is the way to fulfil this request. While tools like Flow Orchestration exist, the standard and most robust way to handle complex, criteria-based routing for record sign-offs is an approval process: it can hold many approval steps, each with its own step entry criteria - Step 1 routing to Leader A if the region is North, Step 2 to Leader B if the region is South and the discount is over 20%, and so on - so with 30 potential sets of criteria the process identifies the correct approver automatically, with a clear audit trail of who approved what and why.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a button that opens an email template to the correct leader) — prone to human error, since the salesperson might select the wrong leader, and it leaves no approval record.
Option C (a record-triggered flow orchestration) — a flow can launch an approval, but the complex multi-step routing logic is best managed within the approval engine itself for the audit trail it keeps.
Option D (a screen flow where the seller picks the criteria) — a manual form with the same wrong-leader risk as the email button, and no formal sign-off tracking.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.approvals_create_entrycriteria.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.workflow_limits.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters has the Case object set to private. The support manager raised a concern that reps have a broader view of data than expected and can see all cases on their group's dashboards. What is causing reps to have inappropriate access to data on dashboards?
explanation:
The dashboard's running user is what is causing the broader access. A dashboard's running user determines which data is displayed to anyone viewing it: if it is configured with a static running user such as a support manager with View All, every viewer sees the manager's level of data regardless of their own sharing, which bypasses the Private organization-wide default on Case. The fix is to convert it to a dynamic dashboard that runs as the logged-in user, so each viewer's components filter by their own sharing rules and record ownership.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Dashboard Filters) — narrow what a dashboard shows; they cannot widen a viewer's access beyond their sharing.
Option B (Public Dashboards) — folder visibility controls who can open the dashboard, not whose data it displays.
Option D (Dashboard Subscriptions) — deliver a scheduled copy of the dashboard; the data in it is still governed by the running user, so subscriptions are a symptom, not the cause.

question: A Platform Administrator at Universal Containers needs an automated way to delete records based on field values. Which automated solution should the administrator use?
explanation:
Flow Builder is the automated solution for deleting records based on field values. A schedule-triggered flow can run at set intervals (daily at midnight, say) to find records meeting criteria - such as leads that have been Unqualified for over a year - and use the Delete Records element to remove them. For recurring, criteria-based deletion it is the recommended tool.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Automation Studio) — a Marketing Cloud tool, not a core platform feature for record management.
Option C (Mass Delete Records) — a manual administrative tool in Setup; it cannot be scheduled or automated on complex field-level logic.
Option D (Flow Orchestration) — built for complex, multi-user business processes, not simple data cleanup.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_schedule.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.admin_massdelete.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks has a request from the finance team that all won opportunities over a certain value must be checked for accuracy before the deal can be considered fully closed. The assigned finance team member, as well as the sellers' manager, both must sign off on the deal, with the manager doing so first. Then, the finance team member must sign off, for a total of up to three sign-offs per opportunity. How should the administrator address this request?
optionA: Create a screen flow that runs anytime an opportunity is closed.
optionB: Add a Lightning web component to the opportunity page to capture the details in an approval record.
optionC: Create a quick action to send emails to both the manager and the finance team member.
optionD: Create an approval process with specific steps.
explanation:
Creating an approval process with specific steps is the standard and most effective way to manage a structured, multi-step sign-off. Step 1 routes the request to the seller's manager; only after the manager approves does the record move to Step 2, which routes to the specific finance team member - so the manager-first order is strictly enforced. The Approval History related list then gives the finance team a native audit trail showing every signature was obtained before the deal was finalised.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a screen flow that runs when an opportunity is closed) — lacks the record locking, ordered steps and formal status tracking the approval engine provides.
Option B (a Lightning web component capturing details in an approval record) — significant custom code for a process that standard click-not-code configuration handles.
Option C (a quick action emailing the manager and finance member) — an email is not a sign-off; nothing enforces the order or records the approvals.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.what_are_approvals.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_step_approver.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Users at DreamHouse Realty are only allowed to see opportunities they own. Leadership wants an enterprise- wide dashboard of all open opportunities in the pipeline so that users can see how the company is performing at any point in time. How should a Platform Administrator create the dashboard without changing any sharing settings?
optionA: Create a dashboard with the running user set as someone who can see all opportunities.
optionB: Add a filter to the dashboard to filter the opportunities by owner role.
optionC: Build individual dashboards for profiles that need to see the enterprise results.
optionD: Update the dashboard folder settings to manager for the sales reps role.
explanation:
Creating the dashboard with the running user set as someone who can see all opportunities is how to do it without changing sharing. A dashboard can run as a specified user, and that user's security settings determine what every viewer sees; setting the running user to someone with View All or high enough in the role hierarchy to see all records creates a static dashboard that shows company-wide totals and charts to users whose own record access is Private. Viewers cannot click into records they do not own, but the summarised pipeline is visible to all.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (filter the dashboard by owner role) — a filter narrows the data; with the dashboard still respecting each viewer's sharing, reps would see only their own opportunities.
Option C (individual dashboards per profile) — multiplies maintenance and still shows each viewer only what their sharing allows.
Option D (set the dashboard folder to Manager for the sales reps role) — folder access affects who can open the dashboard, not the data displayed within it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.dashboards_view_as.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Platform Administrator at Ursa Major Solar imported records into an object by mistake. Which two tools should the administrator use to undo this import?
explanation:
Data Loader and Mass Delete Records are the two tools for undoing a mistaken import, because undoing it means deleting the incorrectly created records. Mass Delete Records is a browser-based tool in Setup that deletes up to 250 records at a time, or uses criteria to identify and remove larger sets - the quickest route for smaller mistakes. For large-scale errors, Data Loader takes the success file generated during the original import (which contains the new record IDs) and performs a Delete operation.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Weekly Data Export) — a backup tool; it cannot remove existing data from the system.
Option C (Data Import Wizard) — adds or updates data but has no delete function.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.admin_massdelete.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters uses a custom Invoice object to collect customer payment information from an external billing system. The Billing System field needs to be filled in on every Invoice record. How should a Platform Administrator ensure this requirement?
optionA: Create a flow to update the field.
optionB: Require the field on the record type.
optionC: Define an approval process for the field.
explanation:
Making the field universally required is how to ensure the Billing System field is populated on every Invoice record regardless of how it is created - manually, via the API or through an integration. When a field is marked Required in Object Manager, the database rejects any attempt to save a record with that field empty, which is the most robust way to maintain data integrity for a field essential to reporting and external-system alignment.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a flow to update the field) — reactive rather than preventative; it does not stop a record being saved without the value.
Option B (require the field on the record type) — layout-level requirement helps manual entry, but it does not prevent records being created without the data via the API or background processes.
Option C (an approval process for the field) — approvals govern sign-off on a record; they do not enforce that a field has a value.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.custom_field_attributes.htm&language=en_US&type=5
