question: A Platform Administrator needs to create a new prompt template to automatically summarize customer cases for a sales team. The administrator wants to dynamically populate the response with data from the case record. What should the administrator use to display real Salesforce data in an agent response from a prompt template?
explanation:
Merge Fields are what displays real Salesforce data in an agent response from a prompt template. In Prompt Builder, merge fields are the most direct way to inject record data into the AI's instructions - much like a mail merge, an administrator references fields from the object in context, such as {!$Input:Case.Subject} or {!$Input:Case.Description}, and at run time the placeholders are replaced with the actual data from the case being viewed. That gives the AI the grounding it needs to generate an accurate and relevant summary.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Flow) — can ground a prompt with more complex data retrieval, but merge fields are the standard, low-code tool for simple record-to-prompt population.
Option B (Picklists) — a field type; picklists do not populate a prompt with record data.
Option C (Agent Instructions) — provide the how-to logic for the AI; they are not dynamic data points from the database.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.prompt_builder_ground_merge_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Platform Administrator is creating a new action instruction for an agent. This action, named createCase, is designed to generate a new Salesforce Case record based on the user's conversation with the agent. Which set of Action Instructions should the administrator use for the createCase action, according to best practices for action instructions?
optionA: "This action provides the ability to create a new case record in the Salesforce system. Its function is to simply save customer information as a record. Use this when the user wants to create a case."
optionB: "Use this action to create a new Salesforce Case record. The goal is to document a customer's issue in the system. Use this when the user's intent is to create a formal record of their problem or question."
optionC: "Creates a new case record in the system for any type of customer inquiry. The purpose of this is to ensure a record of the interaction is saved."
optionD: "The createCase code snippet is configured to create a case. It runs in the background to handle the user' s request to log a new issue. Its purpose is to solve the customer's issue."
explanation:
The instruction set that defines the action, the goal and the user intent - "Use this action to create a new Salesforce Case record. The goal is to document a customer's issue in the system. Use this when the user's intent is to create a formal record of their problem or question." - is the best choice. Agentforce action-instruction best practices emphasise clarity, intent and specific usage scenarios so the LLM knows exactly when and why to trigger an action; option B gives all three, guiding the agent's reasoning so it does not open a case during a simple inquiry.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A ("provides the ability to create a new case… Use this when the user wants to create a case") — describes the mechanism ("simply save customer information") and gives a circular trigger, so the agent has no real guidance on intent.
Option C ("Creates a new case record for any type of customer inquiry") — too broad: "any type of inquiry" invites the agent to create cases for questions that need none.
Option D ("The createCase code snippet… runs in the background… Its purpose is to solve the customer's issue") — focuses on technical implementation rather than functional business context, and misstates the purpose (logging an issue is not solving it).
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_instructions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: DreamHouse Realty regularly processes customer requests for warranty work and would like to offer customers a self-serve option to generate cases. Which two solutions should an administrator use to meet this request? Choose 2 answers.
explanation:
Web-to-Case and Email-to-Case are the two solutions, because both let a customer raise a case without a rep touching anything.
Web-to-Case gathers support requests from your own website: you enable the feature, choose the case fields to expose, generate the HTML form from the Web-to-Case HTML Generator in Setup, and put that form on your site. Every submission creates a case.
Email-to-Case turns messages sent to your support addresses into cases automatically, populating case fields from the email.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Case Escalation) — acts on a case that has been open too long; it gives the customer no way to create one.
Option C (Case Queues) — hold cases once they exist so a team can pick them up; not a self-service channel.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.setting_up_web-to-case.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.setting_up_email-to-case.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The VP of Sales at Cloud Kicks is receiving an error message that prevents them form saving an Opportunity. The administrator attempted the same edit without receiving an error. How can the administrator validate the error the user is receiving?
explanation:
Logging in as the user is how the administrator validates the error. When an error reproduces for one user and not for the administrator, the difference is in that user's own access, and the way to see it is to log in as them: Log In as Another User puts the administrator into the user's session with their profile, permission sets, role and sharing in force, so the same edit throws the same error and the message can be read directly.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (edit the page layout) — might eventually explain a cause, but it does not reproduce the error, and until it is reproduced there is nothing to diagnose.
Option B (view the setup audit trail) — records administrative changes, not the validation or access failure a user just hit.
Option D (review the sharing model) — inspects the org rather than the user's experience; like the layout, it may explain but cannot reproduce.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.logging_in_as_another_user.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The administrator at Ursa Major Solar need to make sure the unassigned cases from VP customers get transferred to the appropriate service representative within 5 hours. VIP Customers have access to support 24 hours a day. How should this be configured?
explanation:
Escalation Rules are the time-based tool: a rule entry fires when a case has gone unresolved for a set age, and its escalation actions can reassign the case to a rep or a queue and email the people who need to know. That covers both halves of this requirement - the five-hour clock and the transfer to the right representative.
Business hours matter here as a supporting setting rather than the answer. Escalation ages are measured against business hours, so VIP customers entitled to support around the clock need a 24-hour business hours record attached to the rule, otherwise the five-hour clock would pause overnight.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Assignment Rules) — only run when the case is created or reassigned, so they cannot act on elapsed time.
Option B (Business Hours) — a supporting setting the escalation rule measures against; on its own it transfers nothing.
Option C (Case Queues) — a place to hold cases, not a mechanism that moves them after five hours.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.rules_escalation_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.customize_supporthours.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Currently, when support reps at Ursa Major Solar close a case, they manually send an email notification to the customer. The support manager would like to automate this process, as too many reps are forgetting this step. Which two settings should the administrator use to meet this request? (Choose 2).
optionA: Auto-response rule step set for status of closed
optionB: Notify Contact checkbox on close page layout
optionC: Case Close Template in the Support Settings
optionD: Add the Knowledge component to the closed layout
explanation:
The Notify Contact checkbox on the close page layout and the Case Close Template in Support Settings are the two settings, and they work as a pair. Closing a case can send the customer an email without any automation being built for it: on the Close Case page layout, Notify Contact is the checkbox the rep sees at close time, and Salesforce Help states that if there is a contact on the case, selecting Notify contact on case close sends an email to the contact based on a predefined case close template. That template is the second half - Support Settings carries the Case Close Template field, which names the email template used.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (auto-response rule for status Closed) — auto-response rules reply to inbound web and email cases as they arrive, not to a status change on close.
Option D (Knowledge component on the closed layout) — surfaces articles for the rep and sends nothing to the customer.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.closing_cases.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.customize_supportrules.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Dreamhouse realty wants to offer a form on its experience cloud site where inspectors will submit findings from a property inspection. Which feature should an administrator place on the page to fulfill this requirement?
explanation:
A Screen Flow is the feature to place on the Experience Cloud page. A screen flow creates a form that collects user input and performs actions based on that input: screen components display the questions and instructions to the inspector, and flow logic then creates or updates the inspection records or sends notifications. It is the declarative way to put a data-entry form on a site page.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Related List) — displays records related to the current one; it is not a form for collecting new findings.
Option B (Autolaunched Flow) — runs with no user interface, so it cannot present a form for the inspector to fill in.
Option C (Record Detail) — shows the fields of an existing record; it does not guide a visitor through submitting findings.
References:
https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/screen-flows/get-started-with-screen-flows
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.create_forms_with_screen_flow_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The CTO of AW Computing has defined a new policy for cases to improve customer satisfaction. All cases submitted with a Case Reason of Installation must be acknowledged immediately via email and assigned to the appropriate agents. Any cases that are still in the New status after 4 hours must be escalated to support management. What case management tools need to be utilized for this requirement?
explanation:
Auto-response rules, Queues and Escalation Rules are the three tools, because the requirement has three separate jobs.
Auto-response rules send the immediate acknowledgement. They match an incoming case against criteria - here a Case Reason of Installation - and reply to the contact with an email template as the case is created.
Queues are how the case reaches the right agents. A queue holds cases for a group of users who can then take ownership, which is what "assigned to the appropriate agents" means in practice; an assignment rule routes the case into that queue.
Escalation rules handle the four-hour clock. A rule entry ages the case from creation, and its escalation actions reassign it and email support management once the threshold passes.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Auto-response rules, Macros, Entitlements) — a macro is a manual shortcut a rep runs, so it cannot fire on its own after four hours, and entitlements define the level of support owed rather than routing or escalating a case.
Option B (Auto-response rules, Queues, Macros) — right on the first two, but a macro cannot do the timed escalation.
Option D (Auto-response rules, Entitlements, Escalation Rules) — entitlements do not get the case to the right agents; a queue does.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.creating_assignment_rules.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.rules_escalation_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.users_queue_membership_list.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The administrator for AW Computing is working with a user who is having trouble logging in to salesforce. What should the administrator do to identify why the user is unable to login?
explanation:
Reviewing the Login History is how to identify why the user cannot log in, because it is the record of what actually happened when the user tried to sign in. Monitor Login History describes it as the place an admin can monitor every attempt to log in to Salesforce and to Experience Cloud sites, holding up to 20,000 records covering the past six months.
What makes it the diagnostic tool is the Status column. Each attempt carries a login status code naming the reason it failed - wrong password, restricted IP, outside login hours, failed identity verification - alongside the timestamp, the source IP address, the browser and the login type. That turns "the user cannot log in" into a specific cause.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (review the security token) — a security token matters only for API and email client logins, not a browser sign-in.
Option B (review the password history) — describes past passwords the user cannot reuse, not this user's failed attempts.
Option C (review the password policies) — the rules in force for everyone; they are something to check after the history tells you where to look.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.users_login_history.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to encourage employees to choose secure and appropriate passwords for their Salesforce accounts. Which three password policies should an administrator configure? Choose 3 answers.
optionC: Require use of Password Manager App
explanation:
Maximum invalid login attempts, password complexity requirements and number of days until expiration are the three configurable policies. Set Password Policies covers what an admin can actually configure at org level: password history, length and complexity requirements, expiration, and what happens when someone forgets or mistypes a password. Maximum invalid login attempts sets how many wrong passwords are tolerated before the account locks. Password complexity requirements govern the mix of character types a password must contain. Number of days until expiration forces a periodic change.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (prohibited password values) — while Salesforce does block a small set of weak passwords, a list of prohibited values is not one of the configurable password policies in Setup.
Option C (require use of a Password Manager App) — there is no such setting.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.admin_password.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_password_policies.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Dreamhouse Reality just announced its new home concierge offering. This product is unlike anything the company has offered in the past and follows a different business model. What Should the administrator Configure to meet this requirement?
explanation:
Creating a new sales process is what the administrator should configure. A sales process is the ordered set of opportunity stages a deal moves through, and record types exist precisely so one org can run more than one of them: Salesforce describes record types as the way to offer different business processes, picklist values and page layouts to different users. So a genuinely different business model gets its own sales process, with its own stage values, paired with a record type that assigns it to the people selling the concierge offering; existing opportunities keep the original process untouched.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (create a quick action) — creates or updates a record; it does not change the stages a deal travels through.
Option B (create a new approval process) — routes something for sign-off; nothing to do with the sales stages.
Option D (create a new Opportunity product) — a line item on a deal, not a business process.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.customize_recordtype.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud kicks needs to ensure appropriate shipping details are used in orders. Reps should have a streamlined solutions to update the shipping address on selected orders associated with an account when the shipping address is changed on the account. How should the administrator deliver this requirement?
optionA: An autolaunched flow on the order page that updates all open orders shipping addresses whenever the account shipping addresses changes.
optionB: An autolaunched flow on the account page that updates all open orders shipping addresses whenever the account shipping addresses changes.
optionC: A screen flow on the order page that lets the reps choose the updated account shipping address in all open associatedorders
optionD: A screen flow on the account page that lets the reps choose the updated account shipping address in all open associated orders
explanation:
A screen flow on the account page that lets the reps choose the updated account shipping address in all open associated orders is the answer, and the word that decides it is "selected". Reps are not updating every open order, they are choosing which ones to update, and a choice needs a screen. Placed on the Account page - the record where the address actually changed - the flow can query the account's open orders, present them for selection, and write the new shipping address to the ones the rep picks.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (autolaunched flow on the order page updating all open orders) — an autolaunched flow has no user interface, so it would update every matching order with no chance to exclude any, and the order page is the wrong context for a change made on the account.
Option B (autolaunched flow on the account page updating all open orders) — right record, wrong tool: no screen means no selection.
Option C (screen flow on the order page) — the rep would be on one order at a time, which is the opposite of updating a chosen set in one pass.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.create_forms_with_screen_flow_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_record.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Ursa Major Solar has a path on Case. The Company wants to require its users to follow the status values as they are on the path. Agents should be prohibited from preventing the case back to a previous status. Which Feature Should an administrator use to fulfill this request?
explanation:
Validation rules are the feature that enforces the status order. Path displays the stages and guides reps through them, but it does not enforce anything - a user can still set Status back to an earlier value, and Path will happily show them there. Enforcement is a validation rule that compares the new value against the old one: because PRIORVALUE and ISCHANGED are available in validation formulas, a rule can detect that Status moved from a later step to an earlier one and block the save with an error.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Global Value Picklists) — a global value set standardises which values exist across fields but imposes no order and cannot refuse a save.
Option C (Predefined field Values) — pre-populate a field on a quick action; they say nothing about the direction of travel between values.
Option D (Dependent Picklists) — filter one picklist by another's value, which is about available choices, not about moving backwards through them.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_rules_tips.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Human resources department at Northern Trail outfitters wants employees to provide feedback about the manager using a custom object in Salesforce. It is important that managers are unable to see the feedback records from their staff. How should an administrator configure the custom object to meet this requirement?
optionC: Set the default external access to private.
explanation:
Unchecking Grant Access Using Hierarchies on the custom object is the configuration that meets the requirement. That setting determines whether access to records of the custom object is granted through the role hierarchy; with it unchecked, managers do not automatically see records their subordinates own, so feedback records stay hidden from the managers they are about unless access is given by other means such as sharing rules or manual sharing. It is available only on custom objects, which is why the feedback object can be configured this way while standard objects cannot.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (a criteria-based sharing rule) — sharing rules only ever open access up; they cannot take away the visibility the hierarchy grants.
Option C (default external access set to Private) — governs what external (community) users see; managers are internal users reached through the hierarchy, which this setting does not touch.
Option D (an owner-based sharing rule) — like any sharing rule, it grants more access rather than removing the manager's.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_controlling_access_using_hierarchies.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Sales reps at Northern Trail Outfitters have asked for a way to change the Probability field value of their Opportunities. What should an administrator suggest to meet this request?
optionA: Define a new Stage picklist value.
optionB: Create a custom field on Opportunity.
optionD: Make the field editable on page layouts
explanation:
Making the field editable on page layouts is what the administrator should suggest. Probability is a standard field on Opportunity that Salesforce populates from the stage - each stage value carries a default probability, and moving the stage overwrites the field. It is not, however, read-only: adding Probability to the page layout as an editable field lets reps type their own number over the stage-derived default. Note that a later stage change writes the default back, so a manual value survives only until the deal moves.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (define a new Stage picklist value) — changes the process rather than making the existing field editable.
Option B (create a custom field on Opportunity) — would sit beside the standard one and be ignored by forecasting.
Option C (configure Forecasting support) — forecasting consumes the probability and forecast category; it does not control whether reps can edit the field.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_layout.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.faq_forecasts_category_mapping.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An administrator at Cloud Kicks wants to deactivate a User who has left the company. What are two reasons that would prevent a user from being deactivated? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: The use is part of a territory hierarchy.
optionB: The User is in a Custom hierarchy field.
optionC: The User is assigned in workflow email alert.
optionD: The User is the highest role in the role hierarchy
explanation:
The user being in a custom hierarchy field and the user being assigned in a workflow email alert are the two blockers, and Salesforce's considerations for deactivating users name both. A user selected in a custom hierarchy field cannot be deactivated - the save fails with "Cannot inactivate user that is the value of a hierarchy field" - and the block persists even if the field is deleted, until the field is permanently erased. A user who is the sole recipient of a workflow email alert is likewise blocked.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (part of a territory hierarchy) — prevents nothing: deactivating a user removes them from their territories automatically.
Option D (highest role in the role hierarchy) — no obstacle either; the role is simply left without an active user.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_deactivate_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000386275&language=en_US&type=1

corrected.note: Checked against the official considerations for deactivating users. A custom hierarchy field and a sole workflow-email-alert recipient are both documented blockers; territory membership is explicitly not one, since deactivation removes territory assignments by itself.

question: The events manager at dream house realty has a hot lead from a successful open house that needs to become a contact with an associated opportunity. How should this be accomplished from the campaign keeping the associated campaign member history?
optionA: Delete the lead and create a new contact and opportunity.
optionB: Clone the lead and convert the cloned record to a contact.
optionC: Convert the lead from the campaign member detail page.
optionD: Add a contact from a campaign member detail page.
explanation:
Converting the lead from the campaign member detail page is documented behaviour: Displaying and Editing a Campaign Member states that if the campaign member is based on a lead, you can convert the lead from that page. That route matters because of what it preserves. Conversion produces the account, contact and opportunity, and the existing campaign member record is carried over to the new contact, so the person's membership and status history stay attached to the campaign rather than being lost with the lead.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (delete the lead and create a new contact and opportunity) — deleting the lead destroys the campaign member record with it.
Option B (clone the lead and convert the clone) — the clone has no campaign history behind it.
Option D (add a contact from the campaign member detail page) — produces a fresh membership dated today, which is not the same as the history from the open house.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.campaigns_members_detail.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.customize_mapleads.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: AW Computing has added a new custom text field called Market Segment on the Lead object. When a Lead is converted, the new field is not getting copied to the Account record. What should the administrator do to ensure the Market Segment field from a Lead is copied to the converted Account record in routine?
optionA: Ensure the Market Segment field on the Lead is mapped to right field on Account.
optionB: Ensure Account has a field that has the exact same name as the new Lead field.
optionC: Write a Validation Rule to ensure the Account has a value in that field.
optionD: Write a record-triggered flow to copy the custom field from Lead to Account.
explanation:
Ensuring the Market Segment field on the Lead is mapped to the right field on Account is what makes the value copy on conversion routinely, with no manual intervention. The Lead Field Mapping tool under Lead Settings (Map Lead Fields) maps custom fields on Lead to custom fields on Account, Contact or Opportunity so the data is transferred when leads are converted - for example Market Segment on Lead to Market Segment on Account.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (an Account field with exactly the same name) — matching names do nothing by themselves; only an explicit mapping carries the value across.
Option C (a validation rule requiring the Account field) — would block saves that lack the value, not populate it from the Lead.
Option D (a record-triggered flow copying the field) — unnecessary code-like automation for something the standard lead field mapping already does.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.customize_mapleads.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.customize_mapleads_guidelines.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: New Leads needs to be routed to the correct sales person based on the lead address. How should the administrator configure this requirement?
explanation:
Lead assignment rules are the routing mechanism. Set Up Assignment Rules describes them as conditions that determine how leads or cases are processed, assigning each to a specified user or queue. For this requirement the rule entries test address fields - City, State/Province, Country, or postal code ranges - and send matching leads to the rep who owns that territory. Entries are evaluated in order, so the first match wins and a final catch-all entry can hold anything that fits no rule.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (create a formula field) — derives a value for display; it assigns nothing.
Option C (assign with an escalation rule) — escalation rules act on cases after time has passed, not on new leads.
Option D (configure a validation rule) — can only block a save; it cannot route a record.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.creating_assignment_rules.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.customize_leadrules.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Ursa Solar Major is evaluating Salesforce for its service team and would like to know what objects were available out of the box. Which three of the standard objects are available to an administrator considering a support use case? Choose 3 answers.
explanation:
Contract, Case and Account are the three standard objects available out of the box for a support use case. Standard objects ship with Salesforce; custom objects are ones you build. All three are ordinary parts of a support implementation - the customer, the issue being worked, and the agreement that governs the level of service owed.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option C (Ticket) — not a Salesforce object at all; it is the name other help desk products use for what Salesforce calls a Case, which is why it makes a good distractor for an evaluator arriving from another tool.
Option D (Request) — the same: another product's term, not a standard Salesforce object.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.basics_object_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.cases_intro.htm&language=en_US&type=5
_cat: Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

question: A Sales user is trying to manage Campaign Members for an upcoming networking event. The user can view the Campaign, but add new Campaign Members or update Member statuses. How can an administrator troubleshoot this problem?
optionA: Create a permission set to allow the user to edit Campaign Members.
optionB: Provide the user access to both Leads and Contacts to edit all Members.
optionC: Make sure the Marketing User Checkbox is checked on the user record page.
optionD: Run a Campaign report and update any Member information via Data Loader.
explanation:
Making sure the Marketing User checkbox is checked on the user record is the fix, because campaign management is gated by a checkbox on the user record rather than by object permissions alone. Who has access to Campaigns? sets out the split: depending on sharing, users can view campaigns, view the advanced campaign setup, or run campaign reports, but only designated marketing users get to create and manage them. So a user who can see the campaign but cannot add members or change member statuses is almost always missing the Marketing User checkbox. Note that the checkbox works alongside ordinary permissions rather than replacing them - the user still needs read and edit access to campaigns and to the leads or contacts being added.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a permission set allowing Campaign Member edits) — cannot substitute, because this is a user-record attribute rather than an object permission.
Option B (access to both Leads and Contacts) — granting more access to leads and contacts does not unlock campaign member management.
Option D (update members via Data Loader) — works around the symptom instead of fixing the user's access.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.faq_campaigns_who_has_access.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.campaigns_members_landing_page.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Sales and Customer Care at Ursa Major Solar need to see different fields on the Case related list from the Account record. Sales users want to see Case created date and status while Customer Care would like to see owner, status, and contact. What should the administrator use to achieve this?
explanation:
The Page Layout editor is what the administrator uses, because related list columns are a page layout property. In the page layout editor you open the Cases related list's properties and choose which fields appear as columns, in what order, and how the rows sort. Because each layout carries its own version of that related list, assigning one layout to Sales and another to Customer Care gives each team its own column set on the same Account page - created date and status for one, owner, status and contact for the other.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Related Lookup Filters) — restrict which records a lookup field will accept; they do not choose related list columns.
Option B (Compact Layout Editor) — compact layouts drive the highlights panel and mobile preview, not related lists.
Option D (Search Layout Editor) — search layouts control result and list columns for search, not the related list on a record page.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_layout.htm&language=en_US&type=5
_cat: Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

question: An administrator at AW Computing has been asked to help the Support team with report folders. They want a folder called Support Reports and two folders underneath called Helpdesk and R&D. The Support organization uses public groups for Support Agents, R&D, and Managers. Support agents should be able to run Helpdesk reports, but should not be able to view R&D reports. Support managers should be able to view and edit all reports. Which two ways should these folders be shared? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Share the R&D folder with Support Managers with Edit Access.
optionB: Share the Helpdesk folder with Support Agents with View access.
optionC: Share the Support Reports folder with Support Managers with Edit Access.
optionD: hare the Support Reports folder with Support Agents with View Access.
explanation:
Sharing the Helpdesk folder with Support Agents at View access and sharing the Support Reports folder with Support Managers at Edit access are the right pair. Report folder access is granted per folder, to public groups, roles or territories, at View, Edit or Manage level - and it does not cascade, since report folders in Lightning are a flat list rather than a true hierarchy. Each folder has to be shared on its own terms. Sharing Helpdesk with Support Agents at View lets them run those reports without touching R&D; sharing Support Reports with Support Managers at Edit gives managers the run-and-modify rights they were asked for.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (share the R&D folder with Support Managers at Edit) — managers' access is already covered by the Support Reports share, and this does nothing about what agents may see.
Option D (share the Support Reports folder with Support Agents at View) — an attempt to grant access by containment; it does not scope agents to Helpdesk and, if access did flow, would expose R&D.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.access_report_folders.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.analytics_sharing_permissions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Administrator supporting global team of salesforce users has been asked to configure the company settings. Which two options should the administrator configure? Choose 2 answers.
explanation:
Default Language and Currency Locale are the two company settings to configure, because Company Settings is where org-wide defaults for a global user base live. Manage Information About Your Company describes the Company Information page as holding the org's key attributes, default language, default locale and currency among them. Default Language sets the language of labels, buttons, tabs and help text for everyone who has not overridden it personally. Currency Locale sets the corporate currency and the format numbers and currency fields take. Both are exactly the sort of thing a global rollout has to settle centrally.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Login Hours) — a security setting configured per profile, not a company setting.
Option B (Password Policy) — a security setting under Security Controls, not part of Company Settings.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.company_information_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.setting_the_fiscal_year.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers requires a different Lightning page to be displayed when Accounts are viewed in the Sales Console and in the Service Console. How should an administrator meet this requirement?
optionC: Assign Lightning pages as app default.
explanation:
Assigning Lightning pages as app default is the whole answer. A Lightning record page is assigned, and one of the things you can assign it to is an app: activating a record page offers Org Default, App Default, and an App, Record Type and Profile combination - so the same object can render one page inside the Sales Console and a different one inside the Service Console. Setting each page as the app default for its own console needs no other configuration.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (update page layout assignments) — page layout assignments govern fields and related lists by profile and record type, not which Lightning page renders.
Option B (define multiple record types) — would force an artificial data distinction to achieve a display difference.
Option D (create different user profiles) — would split users who may well need both apps.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.lightning_page_overview.htm&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_app_builder_customize_lex_pages_activate.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5
_cat: Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

question: Cloud Kicks has decided to delete a custom field. What will happen to the data in the field when it is deleted?
optionA: The data in the field is stored for 15 days.
optionC: The data associated with the field is required.
optionD: The data is restorable from the recycle bin.
explanation:
The data in the field being stored for 15 days is what happens. Deleting a custom field does not destroy its data straight away: the field and its contents move to the Deleted Fields list for that object and stay there for 15 days. During that window you can undelete the field, and its data returns with it, or erase it to hard-delete immediately. After 15 days Salesforce purges it permanently.
Two details worth holding on to: the field keeps counting against the object's custom field limit until it is purged, and it is the Deleted Fields list in Object Manager that holds it - not the record Recycle Bin.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (the data is permanently deleted) — only after the 15-day window, or if the administrator explicitly erases it.
Option C (the data associated with the field is required) — deletion has nothing to do with a field being required; the statement does not describe any behaviour.
Option D (restorable from the recycle bin) — the Recycle Bin holds deleted records; a deleted field is restored from the Deleted Fields list in Object Manager.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.fields_managing_deleted_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
_cat: Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

corrected.note: The answer was right but its text was not: Salesforce retains a deleted custom field and its data for 15 days, not 20, and recovery is from the Deleted Fields list in Object Manager rather than the Recycle Bin. The option and explanation are corrected; the key stays A.

question: The administrator at Cloud Kicks has created an approval process for time off requests. Which two automated actions are available to be added as part of the approval process? Choose 2 answers.
explanation:
Field Update and Email Alert are the two automated actions available. Classic approval processes accept automated actions at four points - initial submission, each approval step, final approval or rejection, and recall - and the actions available are the workflow action types: field updates, email alerts, tasks, and outbound messages. Both are the ones this scenario would use: stamp a status field as the time-off request advances, and mail the requester and the approver.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Chatter Post) — not among the automated actions a classic approval process can attach.
Option C (Auto launched Flow) — not an approval action either; to involve a flow you either move to Flow Approval Processes or have a record-triggered flow react to the field the approval process updated.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.approvals_automated_actions.htm&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.approvals_creating_approval_actions.htm&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.approvals_automated_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_automated_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Administrator wants to trigger a follow-up task for the opportunity owner when they close an opportunity as won, and another task after 60 days to check in with the customer. Which two automation tools should the administrator use? Choose 2 answers.
explanation:
Process Builder and Workflow Rules are the two tools, because both halves of the requirement are "create a task" and these are the two things here that can do that on a schedule. A workflow rule creates the immediate task when the stage becomes Closed Won, and a time trigger - an offset of up to 999 days from a date field on the record - creates the 60-day check-in. Process Builder achieves the same with immediate and scheduled actions on one criteria node.
Worth knowing in practice: Workflow Rules reached end of support on 31 December 2025, and new automation of this shape is built with scheduled paths in Flow Builder.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option C (Field Update) — an action available inside those tools rather than a tool in its own right, and it can only overwrite a field; it cannot create a task.
Option D (Outbound Message) — sends data to an external endpoint; it creates no task.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.workflow_time_dependent.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: A Field Update cannot create a task, so it can never satisfy a requirement whose every step is "create a task" — and it is an action inside an automation tool, not a tool. Process Builder and Workflow Rules are the two options that can create both the immediate and the time-delayed task.

question: Brokers at DreamHouse Realty need to see certain information about one or more cases when referencing the contact record. This record case Name, Case ID, Customer Name, Case Reason, Case Status, and Case Creation Date. Which two changes in Setup should the administrator make?
optionA: Use the page layout editor to change the related list type to Enhanced List.
optionB: Edit the Related List component in the Lightning App Builder and choose Related List as the related list type.
optionC: Edit the Related List component in the Lightning App Builder and choose Enhanced List as the related list type.
optionD: Use the page layout editor to include the appropriate column in the Cases related list.
explanation:
Choosing Enhanced List as the related list type in the Lightning App Builder and adding the appropriate columns in the page layout editor are the two changes, in two different places. The columns themselves come from the page layout editor: edit the Cases related list there and add Case ID, Customer Name, Case Reason and the rest. But a standard related list in Lightning Experience renders only four columns, so the six requested fields will not all appear. Setting the Related List component's Related List Type to Enhanced List in the Lightning App Builder raises the limit to ten columns, and adds column resizing, sorting and text wrapping.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (change the related list type to Enhanced List in the page layout editor) — the related list type cannot be set from the page layout editor at all; it is a property of the Lightning component.
Option B (choose Related List as the type in the Lightning App Builder) — the plain Related List type keeps the four-column cap, so six columns would not show.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_app_builder_create_dynamic_related_list.htm&language=en_US&type=5
_cat: Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

corrected.note: Six fields were requested, and a standard Lightning related list displays at most four columns; Enhanced List raises that to ten. The previously marked plain "Related List" type would silently drop two of the six fields.

question: AW Computing has six sales teams in a region. These teams always consists of the same account manager, engineer, and assistant. What should the administrator configure to make it easier for teams to collaborate with the same customer?
optionA: Enable and configure standard opportunity teams with splits.
optionB: Propose the users manually share all their accounts with their teammates.
optionC: Create a queue for each team and assign account ownership to the queue.
optionD: Enable account teams and show the users how to set up a default account team.
explanation:
Enabling account teams and showing users how to set up a default account team is the configuration, because six teams with a fixed membership is the case account teams were designed for. Enable account teams, then have each user build a default account team of their account manager, engineer and assistant; that team is then added automatically to the accounts they own, with the access level and role each member should have.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (standard opportunity teams with splits) — solve a different problem, crediting revenue across a deal, and would not give collaborative access to the account itself.
Option B (users manually share all their accounts) — puts the same work on people every time an account is created, and nothing keeps it consistent.
Option C (a queue per team owning the accounts) — assigning account ownership to a queue is not possible for accounts, and a queue holds records for claiming rather than sharing them with a standing team.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.accountteam_def.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Sales director at Cloud Kicks wants to be able to predict upcoming revenue in the next several fiscal quarters so they can set goals and benchmark how reps are performing. Which two features should the administrator configure? Choose 2 answers.
explanation:
Forecasting and Opportunity Stages are the two features. Forecasting projects revenue across future fiscal periods, which is what lets a sales director see what is expected to close in coming quarters and measure reps against it. Forecasting rests on Opportunity Stages: each stage carries a probability and maps to a forecast category, and that mapping is what turns an open pipeline into a revenue projection.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Sales Quotes) — customer-facing pricing documents that project nothing (note that quotes are not the same thing as sales quotas).
Option B (Opportunity List View) — shows the records that exist today but makes no prediction about future quarters.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.faq_forecasts_category_mapping.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The marked answer left out Forecasting entirely, which is the one feature that actually predicts revenue by fiscal quarter. Its own explanation argues for Forecasting and Opportunity Stages and never mentions the two options it had marked correct.

question: The administrator at DreamHouse Realty added an email quick action to the Case page layout and is unable to see the action on the case feed. Which feature must be enabled to ensure the quick action will be displayed as expected?
explanation:
Email-to-Case is the feature that must be enabled. Send Email Action Considerations for Cases states the dependency in one line: "Turn on Email-to-Case to enable the case-specific Send Email action on cases." Until Email-to-Case is on, the action can sit on the layout and still not appear in the case feed.
Worth knowing for the exam and for real orgs: enabling Email-to-Case for this purpose does not oblige you to configure routing addresses - the considerations note that this requirement is separate from routing or org-wide addresses.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Email Notifications) — a user preference; not the switch that turns the case Send Email action on.
Option C (Email Alerts) — an automation action that sends mail without any user involvement; unrelated to the quick action appearing.
Option D (Email Templates) — supply the body of a message once the action exists; they do not make it appear.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.case_interaction_send_email_quick_action_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.setting_up_email-to-case.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) is partnering with a used shoe store and second-hand bicycle emporium. CK has an automated business process it wants to run once a week to count the number of open cases related to an account. How should the administrator recommend automating this business process?
optionA: Create a workflow rule with an outbound message.
optionB: Set up a scheduled process in Process Builder.
optionC: Configure a scheduled flow in flow Builder.
optionD: Use a process to update the account when it is edited
explanation:
Configuring a scheduled flow in Flow Builder is the recommendation. Flow Builder supports a schedule-triggered flow that runs at a specified interval - weekly here - and performs actions on every record that meets its criteria, so it can visit each account, count its open cases and record the result, with no user involved.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a workflow rule with an outbound message) — workflow rules fire on record save, not on a weekly schedule, and an outbound message sends data to an external endpoint rather than counting anything.
Option B (a scheduled process in Process Builder) — Process Builder has scheduled actions that follow a triggering record change, not a standalone weekly run, and it is retired for new automation in favour of Flow.
Option D (a process that updates the account when it is edited) — runs only when someone edits the account, which is not once a week and misses accounts nobody touches.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_schedule.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An administrator at Universal Containers is reviewing current security settings in the company's Salesforce org. What should the administrator do to prevent unauthorized access to Salesforce?
optionD: Enable caching and autocomplete on login page
explanation:
Enabling multi-factor authentication is the setting that actually raises the bar against unauthorized access: on top of the password, the user has to present a second factor - an authenticator app, a security key, or a built-in authenticator - so a stolen password alone is not enough. Salesforce turns it on org-wide from Identity Verification in Setup.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (disable TLS requirements for sessions) — would expose sessions that are currently encrypted, moving security backwards.
Option C (customize organization-wide defaults) — governs which records a user can see once they are already inside, not whether the wrong person can get in.
Option D (enable caching and autocomplete on the login page) — makes it easier for the next person at that machine to sign in as the user.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_overview_2fa.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.security_mfa_org_wide_setting.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which tool should an administrator use to review recent configuration changes made in their org?
explanation:
Setup Audit Trail is the record of configuration changes. It names the date, the user, and what was changed; the page shows the 20 most recent entries and the Download link exports the full history for the past 180 days, after which entries are deleted.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Critical Updates) — Release Updates, the feature that replaced Critical Updates, announces changes Salesforce is making to the platform, not changes your administrators made.
Option B (Debug logs) — capture what happened during a single transaction (queries, workflow, Apex), not who changed a setting.
Option D (Field History Tracking) — records changes to field values on records, which is data rather than configuration.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.admin_monitorsetup.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks has a custom object named shoe. The administrator has been asked to ensure that when a relationship is created between Account and shoe to prevent orphaned shoe records. What should the administrator do to complete this requirement?
explanation:
Creating a master-detail relationship is what prevents orphaned Shoe records. An orphan is a child record with no parent, and master-detail is the relationship that makes that impossible: the relationship field on the detail record is required, so a Shoe cannot be saved without an Account, and it cannot later be left dangling - if the Account is deleted, its Shoes are deleted with it rather than surviving without a parent. A plain lookup would allow exactly what the requirement forbids: the field is optional, and deleting the account clears it and leaves the Shoe behind.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (an indirect lookup) — a real relationship type, but it belongs to external objects, linking them to a standard or custom object by an external id.
Option B (an encrypted lookup) — does not exist.
Option C (a hierarchical lookup) — a real relationship type too, but available only on the User object.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5
_cat: Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

question: An administrator created a record trigger flow to update contacts. How should the administrator reference the values of the active record the flow is running on?
optionD: Use the Get Records element to find the Id.
explanation:
The $Record global variable is how a record-triggered flow references the record it is running on. The triggering record is already loaded and available as $Record, so its fields are referenced directly - $Record.Email, $Record.AccountId - with no query of any kind. Its companion is worth knowing: $Record__Prior holds the values the record had immediately before the save, which is how a flow detects that a particular field changed.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (the {!Contact.Id} global variable) — there is no such global variable.
Option B (the {!Account.Id} record variable) — refers to the wrong object entirely.
Option D (a Get Records element to find the Id) — would spend a query retrieving a record the flow was handed for free, which on a before-save flow also loses the performance advantage that makes those flows worth using.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_resources_global_variables.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_record.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An administrator has reviewed an upcoming critical update. How should the administrator proceed with activation of the critical update?
optionA: Activate the critical update in a sandbox.
optionB: Allow the critical update to auto-activate.
optionC: Activate the critical update in production.
optionD: Allow the critical update to auto-activate in a sandbox.
explanation:
Activating the critical update in a sandbox is how to proceed. The safe sequence is to activate the update in a sandbox first, exercise the customizations and integrations that could be affected, and only then let it take effect in production. That is the whole point of the window Salesforce gives you before auto-activation: it is time to test, not time to wait.
One naming note for the current platform: these are now called Release Updates. The Critical Updates node was retired and replaced by Release Updates in Setup, but the guidance is unchanged - test in a sandbox before the enforcement date.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (allow the update to auto-activate) — surrenders the choice of when to find out what breaks, in production.
Option C (activate the update in production) — skips the test.
Option D (allow it to auto-activate in a sandbox) — still leaves the timing to Salesforce rather than testing on your own schedule; the point of the sandbox is to activate deliberately and check.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.release_updates.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Dream house realty needs to use consistent picklist values in the category field on accounts and cases, with values respective to record types. Choose 2 options.
explanation:
Global picklist and Dependent picklist are the keyed pair. The consistency half of this requirement is clear: a global value set is one list of values maintained in one place and shared by picklist fields on more than one object, so the Category field on Account and the Category field on Case draw from the same values and stay in step.
The record type half is where this item is weak, and it is worth knowing why. Making values "respective to record types" is done by record types themselves: Edit Picklists for Record Types and Business Processes describes selecting a record type and editing the picklist field to change which values it offers. A dependent picklist does something different - it filters one picklist by the value chosen in a controlling picklist on the same record, which has nothing to do with record types.
The key is left as the source had it, but treat the second half as unreliable. The mechanism that actually varies values by record type is record-type picklist assignment on the custom picklist field, not a dependent picklist.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Multi-select picklist) — a field type that allows several values at once; it neither shares values across objects nor varies them by record type.
Option D (Custom picklist) — a plain custom picklist on each object would hold its own separate value list, so Account and Case could drift apart; the sharing comes from the global value set, though note that record-type value assignment does happen on the field itself.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.editing_picklists_for_record_types_and_business_processes.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_recordtype_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The item pairs a global value set, which is right for consistency across objects, with a dependent picklist, which does not vary values by record type - record-type picklist assignment does. The key is unchanged because the documentation does not settle which option the source intended as the second answer, but the dependent-picklist half does not support the stem.

question: A user at Cloud Kicks is having issues logging in to Salesforce. The user asks the administrator to reset their password. Which two options should the administrator consider when resetting the user's password? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Resetting the password will change the user's password policy.
optionB: Single sign-on users can reset their own passwords using the forgot password link.
optionC: Resetting a locked-out user's password automatically unlocks the user's account.
optionD: After resetting a password, the user may be required to activate their device to successfully log in to Salesforce.
explanation:
Resetting a locked-out user's password automatically unlocking the account, and the user possibly having to activate their device after the reset, are the two considerations, and Reset Passwords for Your Users lists them word for word.
"Resetting a locked-out user's password automatically unlocks the user's account" - so an admin dealing with a lockout does not have to click Unlock separately; the reset covers it.
"After an admin resets a password, users are sometimes required to activate their devices to successfully log in to Salesforce" - identity verification treats the next login as coming from an unrecognised device and asks the user to confirm it.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (resetting the password changes the user's password policy) — a reset changes one user's password; the password policy is org-level or profile-level configuration and is untouched.
Option B (SSO users can reset their own password via the forgot password link) — the same article rules this out: only an admin can reset SSO user passwords.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.resetting_and_expiring_passwords.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_unlock.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The explanation on this question was about the page layout editor - text belonging to a different item entirely - and never addressed password resets. It has been replaced with the documented considerations, which confirm the existing key.

question: Support agent at Cloud Kicks are spending too much time finding resources to solve cases. The agents need a more efficient way to find documentation and similar cases from the Case page layout. How should an administrator meet this requirement?
optionA: Create a custom object to capture popular case resolutions.
optionB: Use an interview flow to capture Case details.
optionC: Direct users to Global Search to look for similar cases.
optionD: Configure Knowledge with articles and data categories.
explanation:
Configuring Knowledge with articles and data categories is the feature built for this. Articles hold the documented solutions, and data categories classify them, which does two jobs at once: it organises the knowledge base and it controls who may see which articles. The payoff on the Case page is suggested articles: case fields can be mapped to data categories, so when a case is saved Salesforce searches for articles sharing its keywords and floats the ones matching the case's category to the top of the list - agents get candidate solutions without leaving the case.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a custom object to capture popular resolutions) — rebuilds a weaker version of Knowledge with no article lifecycle, no categorisation and no suggestion engine.
Option B (an interview flow to capture case details) — collects details rather than surfacing answers.
Option C (direct users to Global Search) — is what they are already doing too slowly.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.knowledge_whatis.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.category_whatis.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The sales team at Ursa Major Solar has asked the administrator to automate an outbound message. What should the administrator utilize to satisfy the request?
explanation:
A record-triggered flow is what the administrator should use. An outbound message is configured in Setup and then fired by an automation, and Salesforce documents flows as one of the things it can be associated with: outbound messages can be associated with flows, workflow rules, approval processes, or entitlement processes. A record-triggered flow that runs after the record is saved is therefore the current way to automate one.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Case Auto-Response Rule) — sends an email reply to an inbound case and has nothing to do with a SOAP message to an external endpoint.
Option B (Task Assignment) — creates work for a user inside Salesforce; it sends nothing outbound.
Option D (Process Builder) — the distractor to be careful about: it could invoke an outbound message historically, but Salesforce has retired it in favour of Flow, so it is not what an administrator should be told to build today.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.workflow_managing_outbound_messages.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Administrator at Cloud Kicks need to automatically route support cases, regardless of how they are created, to a queue based on case priority. What tool should the administrator use?
explanation:
Assignment Rules are the routing engine for cases, and the phrase that matters in this stem is "regardless of how they are created". An active case assignment rule runs on cases arriving from Web-to-Case, Email-to-Case, the API and On-Demand Email-to-Case, as well as ones created in the UI when the rule is applied - so one rule covers every channel. Each rule holds ordered entries; an entry that tests Priority sends matching cases to the queue for that priority, and the first matching entry wins.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Email-to-Case) — a channel rather than a routing tool: it creates cases, it does not decide who works them.
Option C (Auto-Response Rules) — reply to the customer and change no ownership at all.
Option D (Web-to-Case) — another intake channel, and one that covers only cases from the web form.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.creating_assignment_rules.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.customize_leadrules.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) needs a new sales application. The administrator there is an application package on the AppExchange and wants to begin testing it in a sandbox to see If it addresses CK's needs. What are two considerations when installing a managed package in a sandbox? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Any metadata changes to the package have to be recreated in production.
optionB: The installation link has to be modified to test.saiesiorcc.com.
optionC: Install for Admins Only will be the only Install option available.
optionD: The package will be removed any time the sandbox is refreshed.
explanation:
The installation link having to be changed to the test domain, and the package being removed whenever the sandbox is refreshed, are the two considerations. A package's install URL points at login.salesforce.com, which resolves to production, so to install into a sandbox the administrator replaces login with test in that URL. And because refreshing a sandbox rebuilds it from its source org, a package installed only in the sandbox disappears at the next refresh unless the source org carries it too.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (metadata changes to the package have to be recreated in production) — true of any sandbox work, not specific to installing a managed package.
Option C (Install for Admins Only is the only option) — it is one of three install options, alongside Install for All Users and Install for Specific Profiles.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.distribution_installing_packages.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The explanation names the modified test.salesforce.com install link and the loss of the package on sandbox refresh — B and D. The answer key had C, which is simply false: Install for Admins Only is one of several install options, not the only one.

question: An administrator at Universal Containers needs a simple way to trigger an alert to the director of sales when opportunities reach an amount of $500,000. What should the administrator configure to meet this requirement?
optionA: Set up Big Deal Alerts for the amount.
optionD: Key Deals component on the homepage
explanation:
Setting up Big Deal Alerts for the amount is the simple way. A Big Deal Alert is a standard setting that emails people when an opportunity crosses a threshold - no automation to build and no code. One detail to carry into the exam: the threshold is a pair, not a single number. Set Up Big Deal Alerts for Opportunities has you enter both a trigger amount in the corporate currency and a trigger probability, and the alert fires when an opportunity reaches both. It fires once; if the amount or probability later fall below the threshold and climb back, it fires again.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Opportunity Update Reminders) — scheduled nudges to owners about stale records, not an amount threshold alert.
Option C (opportunity warning in Kanban view) — Kanban alerts flag deals needing attention inside that view only; nothing is sent to the director.
Option D (Key Deals component on the homepage) — there is no such home page component.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.activating_big_deal_alerts.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An administrator at Northern Trail Outfitters is creating a validation rule. Which two functions should the administrator use when creating a validation rule? Choose 2 answers.
explanation:
The error condition formula and the error message location are the two things a validation rule requires. The error condition formula is the test, written so that a result of TRUE means the record is invalid - which trips people up, because the formula describes the condition you want to block, not the one you want to allow. The error message location decides where the message appears: at the top of the page, or attached to a specific field so the user is pointed straight at what to fix.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Formula return type) — something you choose when creating a formula field; a validation rule's result is always a Boolean.
Option D (Rule active date) — there is no active date on a validation rule; it is simply active or inactive.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_rules_tips.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Aw Computing needs to capture a loss reason in rich text field when an opportunity is Closed lost. How should an administrator configure this requirement?
optionA: Select the requirement checkbox next to the loss reason field on the page layout.
optionB: Create a validation rule to display an error if stage is Closed lost and Loss Reason is blank.
optionC: Check the required checkbox on the Loss Reason field in Object Manger.
optionD: Configure a workflow rule to display an error if Loss Reason is blank
explanation:
Creating a validation rule that displays an error if Stage is Closed Lost and Loss Reason is blank is the configuration. The requirement is conditional - Loss Reason is needed only when the Stage is Closed Lost - and that is precisely what a validation rule expresses and nothing else here can: the rule tests for the combination and blocks the save with a message.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (required checkbox on the page layout) — required is unconditional; it would demand a loss reason on every opportunity from the moment it is created, including ones that go on to be won.
Option C (required checkbox in Object Manager) — the same problem, and stricter: it applies to the API as well as the UI.
Option D (a workflow rule to display an error) — a workflow rule cannot display an error or stop a save at all; it acts after the record is saved.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_rules_tips.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks wants to track shoe designs by products. Shoe designs should be unable to be deleted, and there can be multiple designs for one product across various stages. Which two steps should the administrator configure to meet this requirement? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Add a custom master-detail field for shoe designs on the Product object,
optionB: Create a custom object for shoe designs.
optionC: Use the standard object for designs.
optionD: Configure a custom lookup field for shoe designs on the Product object.
explanation:
Creating a custom object for shoe designs and configuring a custom lookup field to it on the Product object are the two steps. There is no standard object for shoe designs, so the first step is a custom object. The second step is the relationship, and the constraint decides it: a lookup leaves each design standing on its own, while still allowing many designs to point at one product and to sit at different stages. Protecting the designs from deletion is then a permissions question - withhold Delete on the object - rather than a relationship question.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a master-detail field for shoe designs) — master-detail would cascade: delete a Product and every design under it is deleted too, which is the opposite of designs that cannot be deleted.
Option C (use the standard object for designs) — no such standard object exists.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
